text:
Jesper Wallstedt picked up his 14th win of the season on his birthday, a 6-2 win in Boston. He is 14-2-3 with a .926 save rate in 19 starts, and he has saved 17.9 goals above expected: that many more goals kept out than the shots he faced would usually allow, 94th percentile among goalies. The Athletic's Michael Russo wrote that his night in Montreal drew a Carey Price comparison.

What makes this convincing is that he is doing it everywhere. He is above league average on low-, medium- and high-danger shots, including .795 on the hardest chances against a league .685, and he has posted a positive number in eight of his last ten starts. Last season he finished 5.8 goals above expected in 35 games, so this isn't coming from nowhere, though no goalie keeps up a pace like this over a full season. He has carried a heavy load, 19 starts already, and NHL.com's Heather Rule reported he is in net again Tuesday against Nashville.
